Slack Events API + interactivity endpoint (handled by Bolt).

Bolt owns signature verification, the ``url_verification`` challenge,
per-workspace token resolution (via the custom ``authorize`` that
bridges to ``IntegrationToken``), and dispatch to the event / action
/ assistant listeners registered in ``app.integrations.slack_bolt_app``.
Point both the Slack *Events* and *Interactivity* Request URLs here.

Inbound Bot Framework endpoint (Activities). JWT auth + dispatch.

The adapter validates the Bot-Framework JWT (the Teams analog of Slack's
signature check) inside ``process_activity``; we just deserialize the
Activity and hand it to the bot's ``on_turn``.

Start the Teams connection: returns a pairing code (admin only).

The admin installs the Unisson Teams app, then messages the bot
``/connect <code>``; the bot claims the code and stores the tenant link.
Teams Status
Disconnect Teams

Inbound Twilio WhatsApp webhook (form-encoded). Acks immediately.

Verifies ``X-Twilio-Signature``, dedups on ``MessageSid``, then either
completes a pending verification (the member echoed their code) or routes the
message to the bound member's org. Twilio retries on a slow response, so the
heavy turn runs in a background task.

Inbound Postmark email webhook (JSON). Acks immediately.

Verifies the shared secret, enforces DMARC, dedups on ``Message-ID``, then
either completes a pending verification or routes the mail to the bound
member's org. Threads by the email's root ``Message-ID``.

Whether the server is configured for each channel + this org's paired count.

"Configured" is derived from the credentials actually needed to operate —
there's no separate enable flag; each provider is always registered and
simply no-ops without these (like Slack without a token).

Import one or many Samsara API keys (admin only).

For each key the backend calls Samsara's ``GET /me`` to learn the
customer's ``samsara_org_id`` + name, upserts ``samsara_accounts``,
and stores the encrypted key. Returns a per-key result so the UI
can show the success/failure for each line of the textarea
independently.

List every known Samsara customer org for this workspace, with
key + assignment counts (admin only).
Fetch one account + all its keys + all assignments (admin only).

Reassign the Unisson customer this Samsara account is linked to
(admin only). The new customer must already exist.

Returns 409 if the target customer is already linked to a
different Samsara account — the
``uq_samsara_accounts_org_customer`` constraint enforces a 1:1
mapping.
Rename a Samsara API key (admin only).

Delete a Samsara API key (admin only). Cascades to any
``samsara_user_keys`` rows that pointed at this key.

Assign a user to one specific key for one account. Upserts on
(user_id, account_id) — picking a new key for the same pair just
swaps the api_key reference, no duplicate row (admin only).

Unassign one user from one account. The underlying key row is
left intact (other users may still hold it). Admin only.

Return the requesting user's own Samsara assignments.

Non-admins use this to see what they have access to — they can't
see assignments belonging to other workspace members, can't import
keys, can't reassign themselves. Admins see the same thing for
themselves but use ``/samsara/accounts`` for the full picture.

each pair is probed via ``GET /v1/payments?count=1`` to confirm
validity. The admin-supplied ``display_name`` is the dedup key —

Import one or many Productboard Public API tokens (admin only).

Each token is validated by calling Productboard's GET /products with it,
then stored encrypted in the org-level pool. There's no identity to
resolve (the Public API exposes none) and no per-token account — admins
assign tokens to users separately. Returns a per-token result so the UI
can show success/failure for each line of the textarea independently.

the last 4 plaintext chars so the UI can mask the rest.
Rename a Productboard API token (admin only).

``productboard_user_keys`` rows that pointed at this token.

Assign a user to one token (admin only). Upserts on user_id — picking a

row.

Unassign one user (admin only). The underlying token row is left intact
(other users may still hold it).

Return the requesting user's own Productboard assignment.

Non-admins use this to see what they have access to — they can't see
other members' assignments, can't import tokens, can't reassign themselves.
